scope: Targeted corrections for the inspected Herglotz, CM-row-sum and polylogarithm-polygamma bridge drafts; not a claim to have audited every source formula.
status_convention: A false statement has an exact counterargument in the specified domain; a missing-proof status records an unsupported conclusion without asserting its negation. A repair-state records corrections already present elsewhere in the inspected snapshot.
numerical_scope: Reported high-precision residuals are supporting evidence, not interval certificates or proofs of independence.

source_locations.section: The collapse criterion and the values J(p/q)

corrections.issue: The denominator-only criterion rad(q)|30 is false. The nearby criterion based only on the real cyclotomic degree is also false. The numerator is essential, and bounded PSLQ does not establish an if-and-only-if about real numbers.
corrections.proposed_correction: Replace both criteria by the exact formal five-term criterion for coprime positive p,q: p^2 is congruent to 1 or -1 modulo q, and q^2 is congruent to 1 or -1 modulo p, with independent signs. Distinguish this formal statement from unproved numerical nonreduction claims.

evidence.description: The same reports give F(n/(n+1)) for every n. Taking n=6 yields a rational-dilogarithm evaluation at 6/7 although rad(7) does not divide 30. The core at 4/17 is (1/2)Li_2(16/17).
At 2/9, the proposed denominator condition holds, but 2^2 is not congruent to plus or minus 1 modulo 9; beta_9(2) is nonzero. At 11/8, 8^2=9 modulo 11 is neither 1 nor -1.
All-conductor kernel theorem plus normalized field-norm separation.

corrections.issue: The assertion that all reducible rational Herglotz values require only Li_2(1/3), Li_2(1/5), and Li_2(2/5) is unsupported numerically and false in the stated formal calculus.
corrections.proposed_correction: Use the constructive rational-core recursion, allowing rational arguments determined by the numerator and denominator. Remove the universal fixed-vocabulary assertion.

evidence.description: The boundary of xi_(4/17) is -2<2> wedge <17>. Every rational linear combination of the three listed dilogarithm symbols has boundary supported only on primes 2,3,5. Logarithm products contribute zero in the pre-Bloch quotient, so the claimed formal vocabulary cannot represent this value.
A rational core is (1/2)[16/17].

source_locations.section: F(2/q): the general theorem, following paragraph

corrections.issue: The blanket claim that the cotangent-square dilogarithm sum cannot simplify for q>=7 includes even denominators, where F(2/q)=F(1/(q/2)) has a logarithmic evaluation.
corrections.proposed_correction: State the reciprocal-integer logarithmic reduction for every even q. For odd q>=7, the new boundary theorem supplies a formal rational-dilogarithm obstruction, not a proof excluding arbitrary numerical identities.

evidence.description: At q=8, F(2/q)=F(1/4), and the report itself supplies its logarithmic formula in Theorem thm:F1q.
For odd q, beta_q(2)=0 exactly when q divides 3 or 5. Thus every odd q>=7 has nonzero formal obstruction.

corrections.issue: The degree phi(q)/2 is assigned to every cotangent-square argument, including indices k that are not coprime to q.
corrections.proposed_correction: For 1<=k<q/2 set q0=q/gcd(k,q). The argument -cot^2(pi*k/q) generates the maximal real subfield of Q(zeta_q0), and has degree phi(q0)/2 for q0>=3.

evidence.description: cot^2(theta)=(1+cos(2theta))/(1-cos(2theta)); this invertible rational transformation gives the same field as cos(2pi*k/q). At q=12,k=3 the argument is -1, of degree 1, rather than phi(12)/2=2.

source_locations.section: The collapse criterion and the values J(p/q)
Further general laws, the values J(p/q)

corrections.issue: The claimed logarithmic classification q in {3,5} omits q=2 and every multiple of 4. The statement that J(1/q) always retains dilogarithms is false for every even q.
corrections.proposed_correction: For q>=2, formal logarithmic reduction holds exactly for q in {2,3,5} or 4|q. Formal rational-dilogarithm reduction additionally includes q=6,10. State that necessity concerns the five-term calculus. Use the explicit analytic formulas for all successful cases.

evidence.description: J(1/2)=pi^2/48+(1/4)log^2(2), corresponding to q=4.
For even m, J(1/m)=pi^2*(m^2-2)/(48*m)+S(m)-S(m/2)/2-S(2*m)/2, where S(n)=sum_(k=1)^(n-1) log^2(2sin(pi*k/n)).
Canonical cyclotomic and rational-prime wedge checks for q<=1000.

corrections.issue: For even q, the definition of W(q) contains the undefined product cot(pi)*Cl_2(pi). Including its continuous limit and also adding the displayed extra -log(2) double-counts the midpoint contribution.
corrections.proposed_correction: Define W_star(q)=sum_(1<=k<q, 2k!=q) cot(2pi*k/q)Cl_2(2pi*k/q). Then (2/q)F_prime(2/q)-(1+log(2))=pi^2*(q^2-4)/(24*q)+W_star(q)-[2|q]log(2). Equivalently include the midpoint limit inside W and remove the separate correction.

evidence.description: Cl_2(pi)=0, Cl_2_prime(pi)=-log(2), and cot(pi+h)=1/h+O(h), so the product tends to -log(2).

Positive Binet derivative quadrature at q=4,6,8,12 agrees with the corrected formula at 65 working digits; the maximum observed absolute residual is about 1.52e-64. Double-counting changes F_prime by (q/2)log(2). This numerical check is supporting evidence, not an interval proof.

corrections.issue: The derivative is described as invariably nonelementary, and W(q) as irreducible, without a proof. The universal assertion already fails at q=4.
corrections.proposed_correction: Remove universal irreducibility language. Record exact reductions such as W_star(4)=0 and F_prime(1/2)=2+pi^2/4. For other denominators, distinguish an explicit Clausen representation from an independence theorem.

evidence.description: After the midpoint is omitted, all remaining cotangents at q=4 are zero. The corrected derivative identity gives F_prime(1/2)=2+pi^2/4.
The positive Binet derivative integral confirms the q=4 identity.

corrections.issue: The displayed cotangent coefficients are asserted to lie in Q(zeta_q)^+, although this need not be true. Their absence from that field also does not prove the nonexistence of a different reduction.
corrections.proposed_correction: Use the valid uniform coefficient field Q(zeta_lcm(4,q))^+ for the displayed real Clausen sum. State any smaller coefficient field only after proof, and remove deductions of numerical nonreduction based solely on these displayed coefficients.

evidence.description: cot(2pi*k/q)=i*(zeta_q^(2k)+1)/(zeta_q^(2k)-1), wherever finite; this lies in the indicated enlarged real field.

For q=3 the proposed smaller real field is Q, while cot(2pi/3)=-1/sqrt(3). Moreover W(3)=-(2/sqrt(3))*Cl_2(2pi/3). The latter Clausen value is positive because it is (sqrt(3)/2)*sum_(m>=0)((3m+1)^(-2)-(3m+2)^(-2)). Thus W(3) is not in the Q-span of the conductor-3 Clausen values.

corrections.issue: Failure of a bounded integer-relation search is promoted to numerical irreducibility of the antisymmetric golden dilogarithm and to a claim of a new independent constant.
corrections.proposed_correction: Retain the exact symmetric-sum identity. State the search precision, coefficient-height bound, and vocabulary for the antisymmetric part, and say that no relation was found in that search. Prove a specified formal boundary obstruction separately if one is desired.

evidence.description: A finite search excludes only coefficients within the verified search bounds; it cannot exclude all rational relations or other functional identities. An unbalanced pre-Bloch element need not lie in the Bloch-group kernel, so vanishing of a rationalized K3 group alone does not settle its reduction.

corrections.issue: The degree-three non-Galois polynomial field H0 is repeatedly identified with a cyclic cubic class field over a quadratic field K. These fields have different absolute degrees.
corrections.proposed_correction: Write L for the totally real cubic subfield and H=K*L for its normal closure. H has degree 6 over Q and degree 3 over K; H/K is the cyclic Hilbert or ring class extension. Use R_L for the regulator of the cubic polynomial field.

evidence.description: A degree-three extension of Q cannot contain the quadratic field K. A non-Galois S3 cubic with quadratic resolvent K has normal closure H=KL of degree six.

source_locations.section: The regulator as a leading L-value

corrections.issue: The leading coefficient is written as R_L without a class-number hypothesis, and attributed to an asserted general abelian Stark theorem in a rank-one-per-place setting.
corrections.proposed_correction: For either nontrivial character chi of Gal(H/K)=C3, with primitive complete finite Euler factors, use Artin induction: L_K(s,chi)=zeta_L(s)/zeta(s). For totally real cubic L this gives L_K(s,chi)=h_L*R_L*s^2+O(s^3). The coefficient is R_L only after h_L=1 is verified. No claimed general Stark theorem is needed for this identity.

evidence.description: Ind_(C3)^(S3)(chi) is the standard two-dimensional representation; the cubic permutation representation is its direct sum with the trivial representation.
zeta_L(s)=-(h_L*R_L/2)*s^2+O(s^3) and zeta(0)=-1/2.
Cogdell, On Artin L-functions: inductivity and zeta factorization.
Dasgupta, Stark's Conjectures, Theorem 3.1.2: zeta_k^*(0)=-h_k R_k/e_k.

For f=x^3-2x^2-3x+1, disc(f)=257 is squarefree. Minkowski gives ideal norm at most (2/9)sqrt(257)<4. Mod 2, f=x^3+x+1 is irreducible. Mod 3, f=(x-1)(x^2+2x+2), with irreducible quadratic; the unique norm-3 prime is principal since Norm(alpha-1)=3. Thus h_L=1 in this case.

source_locations.section: The regulator as a leading L-value, ray modulus and bnrL1
source_locations.anchor: of the narrow ray class group modulo

corrections.issue: The actual conductor of the order-three character is not distinguished from the displayed ray modulus. At D0=257 the character is unramified, and omission of the factors over 2 changes the leading coefficient by a factor of 3.
corrections.proposed_correction: Specify whether L_K is the primitive Artin/Hecke L-function with complete finite Euler factors, or an imprimitive ray-modulus L-function. At D0=257, if the two Euler factors over 2 are omitted, multiply the primitive L-function by 1+2^(-s)+2^(-2s), and multiply its leading coefficient at zero by 3.

evidence.description: The prime 2 splits in Q(sqrt(257)) because 257=1 mod 8. The original cubic polynomial x^3-2x^2-3x+1 reduces to x^3+x+1 modulo 2 and is irreducible; its Frobenius is a 3-cycle. Thus the two character values over 2 are omega and omega^2, and (1-omega*2^(-s))(1-omega^2*2^(-s))=1+2^(-s)+2^(-2s).
This is a convention clarification; the audit does not assert that the report actually ran PARI with the wrong flag. Its recorded normalization is insufficient to determine that.

source_locations.section: The cubic ring-class family, table and observation
Explanation of the exceptional coefficient at n=16

corrections.issue: High-precision fitting of the new Herglotz/regulator coefficients is treated as exact, and their variation is assigned to a Stark-unit index without the required unit-lattice or class-character computation.
corrections.proposed_correction: Mark fitted identities as conjectural until derived from the Kronecker-limit decomposition with the exact class-group coefficients and unit index. For a determinant to equal the field regulator rather than an integer multiple of it, certify that its units generate a subgroup of index one. Keep previously established identities separately attributed.

evidence.description: A determinant of logarithms of independent units equals the regulator times the subgroup index, up to orientation. A small numerical residual and the analytic class-number formula do not by themselves certify this index or the fitted Herglotz coefficients.

corrections.issue: A structural explanation and failed PSLQ searches at a few C5 and C7 examples are promoted to a universal if-and-only-if classification of single-regulator reductions.
corrections.proposed_correction: Retain the representation-theoretic decomposition into character pairs. State the tested C5 and C7 examples and the coefficient-height bounds as numerical evidence. Do not conclude that every possible single-regulator relation is impossible without an exact algebraic or period-independence argument.

evidence.description: Several character pairs explain why several regulator components naturally occur. They do not prove that a particular weighted sum cannot satisfy a further relation. A bounded negative PSLQ result does not prove such independence.

corrections.issue: The displayed bilateral formula omits the sign (-1)^(s+1) on the first polygamma term and is correct as printed only for odd s.
corrections.proposed_correction: Use sum_(m in Z)(m+a)^(-s-1) = ((-1)^(s+1)*psi^(s)(a)+psi^(s)(1-a))/s! for s>=1 and a outside Z.

evidence.description: Split the bilateral sum into m>=0 and m<=-1 and apply the absolutely convergent polygamma series.
The associated article already gives the corrected general formula and its odd-s specialization.

corrections.issue: The main-body ratio and product use a genuinely complex G4((1+i sqrt(15))/4) while giving real right-hand sides.
corrections.proposed_correction: Replace that factor by Re G4((1+i sqrt(15))/4), equivalently by the average at (1+i sqrt(15))/4 and (-1+i sqrt(15))/4.

evidence.description: Write the Fourier parameter as i*r, with r=exp(-pi*sqrt(15)/2)<1/100. In E4=1+240*sum_(n>=1)sigma_3(n)*(i*r)^n, the leading imaginary term is 240*r. Since sigma_3(n)<2*n^3 and 2*sum_(n>=2)n^3*r^n<r for 0<r<=1/100, the tail cannot cancel it. Hence the imaginary part of G4 is nonzero.
The source report correction addendum dated 2026-06-11 explicitly records this correction.
The associated article uses the class-pair average explicitly.

corrections.issue: The norm of (29+12sqrt(5))/44 is stated as 121; 121 is the norm of its numerator.

evidence.description: The associated article explicitly places the norm on the numerator. Its prose can be made completely unambiguous by also giving the norm of the ratio.

source_locations.anchor: corresponding modular forms do not exist

corrections.issue: Vanishing of G4 or G6 at a special lattice is explained by saying the corresponding modular forms do not exist.
corrections.proposed_correction: State that these modular forms exist, but their values vanish at the indicated CM points because of lattice automorphisms: G4(rho)=0 and G6(i)=0.

evidence.description: For a lattice invariant under multiplication by a unit u, the absolutely convergent weight-w lattice sum equals u^(-w) times itself; it is zero if u^w differs from 1. This concerns a value, not the existence of the modular form.

corrections.issue: Negative PSLQ searches are used to state that raw symmetric ratios are irrational and that a cross-class ratio has algebraic degree four.
corrections.proposed_correction: Replace the categorical conclusions by the exact searches performed, or supply independent algebraicity and minimal-polynomial certificates. A proof of degree four requires an annihilating polynomial and an irreducibility or equivalent degree argument.

evidence.description: Failure to find a rational relation to height 10^30 does not establish irrationality. Failure to find a quadratic polynomial to height 10^12 establishes neither algebraicity nor degree four.

source_locations.anchor: tests are blind to such a factor

corrections.issue: The blanket statement that the vanishing tests are blind to the wrong row prefactor is false for a test of the displayed inhomogeneous row-sum formula. The report does not identify which different zero test was actually run.
corrections.proposed_correction: Specify the exact test and its independent inputs. A test of G6(i)=2zeta(6)+(1/60)*sum_rows detects replacement of 1/60 by 1/120; only a common scaling of an independently vanishing complete expression is invisible.

evidence.description: The row sum at i is -120zeta(6). With prefactor 1/60 the expression is zero; with 1/120 it is zeta(6), not zero.

corrections.issue: The report main body omits the minus sign in the equianharmonic identity involving eta(rho)^24.
corrections.proposed_correction: Use E6(rho)^2=-1728*eta(rho)^24=1728*abs(eta(rho))^24 at rho=exp(i*pi/3).

evidence.description: E4^3-E6^2=1728*Delta and Delta=eta^24; E4(rho)=0.
The source report correction addendum explicitly records this sign correction.
The associated article uses the absolute eta value and explains the negative real value of eta(rho)^24.

corrections.issue: The Clausen component is called the odd part of the polygamma grid at every weight.
corrections.proposed_correction: State the parity by weight: Cl_(2k)(-theta)=-Cl_(2k)(theta), while Cl_(2k+1)(-theta)=Cl_(2k+1)(theta). The Clausen component is antisymmetric at even weight and symmetric at odd weight. The Catalan example remains correct.

evidence.description: The definitions use the sine Fourier series at even weight and the cosine Fourier series at odd weight.

source_locations.section: The boundary of the odd-weight Clausen collapse

corrections.issue: The proved reduction at crystallographic angles is stated as a numerical if-and-only-if for all reduced denominators. The displayed character decompositions and bounded PSLQ do not prove the necessity direction.
corrections.proposed_correction: Keep the sufficiency result for q in {1,2,3,4,6} and the exact Dirichlet L-value decompositions at q=5,8,12. State independence of the additional parity-mismatched L-values from zeta(3) as unresolved here, rather than as a theorem.

evidence.description: The identity Cl_3(2pi/5)=-(6/25)zeta(3)+(sqrt(5)/4)L(3,chi_5) shows that the claimed noncollapse at q=5 requires sqrt(5)L(3,chi_5)/zeta(3) to be nonrational. No proof of that assertion is supplied. Negative bounded PSLQ does not prove it.

corrections.issue: The dimension phi(q)/2 is given without specifying the coefficient field and the formal relation quotient. An invertible DFT over a cyclotomic field does not by itself prove numerical Q-linear independence.
corrections.proposed_correction: Define the formal module, coefficient field, and reflection/distribution relations whose quotient is being counted. Distinguish its dimension from the dimension of a numerical period span, and retain DFT transport only over the specified field.

evidence.description: The displayed Fourier matrix has entries in Q(zeta_q), so its invertibility compares dimensions over that field. Additional hypotheses are needed to identify a numerical Q-linear relation space or prove an exact numerical rank.

source_locations.title: Arithmetic properties of the Herglotz function

corrections.issue: The displayed three-term identity is false for the stated untwisted exterior-square values of beta_p.
corrections.proposed_correction: Do not use this identity in the stated untwisted coefficient space. Remove it or replace it by a correctly formulated identity with a specified action or quotient and a proof. The valid inverse and sign symmetries are sufficient for the relation theorem in this continuation.

evidence.description: Take p=7,n=2. Then n/(n+1)=3 modulo 7 and beta_7(3)=-beta_7(2). The printed identity would imply 3 beta_7(2)=0. The all-conductor relation theorem gives beta_7(2) nonzero because 4 is neither 1 nor -1 modulo 7.
In the exact regular-representation model the defect is the nonzero matrix [[0,3,-3],[-3,0,3],[3,-3,0]].
